# Spatial Density using [scider](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/scider.html)

## Setup

#### Installation
[scider](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/scider.html) is hosted on Bioconductor and is available as a development version on GitHub. To install the development version, you can use the following commands in R:

=== "pak (recommended)"
    
    ```r
    pak::pkg_install("bioc::scider") # (1)!
    ```

    1. If you don't have pak, [check it out](https://pak.r-lib.org/). I find it is the best way to manage all your packages.

=== "BiocManager"

    ```r
    if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
        install.packages("BiocManager")
    }

    BiocManager::install("scider")
    ```

=== "GitHub"
    
    ```r
    if (!requireNamespace("devtools", quietly = TRUE)) {
        install.packages("devtools")
    }

    devtools::install_github("ChenLaboratory/scider")
    ```

[SpatialExperiment](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/SpatialExperiment.html) is the main class used as input.
You cannot use original Seurat or AnnData objects. Please install this as well:

=== "pak (recommended)"
    
    ```r
    pak::pkg_install("bioc::SpatialExperiment") # (1)!
    ```

    1. If you don't have pak, [check it out](https://pak.r-lib.org/). I find it is the best way to manage all your packages.

=== "BiocManager"

    ```r
    if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
        install.packages("BiocManager")
    }

    BiocManager::install("SpatialExperiment")
    ```


#### Import libraries

```r
library(scider)
library(SpatialExperiment)
```

## Load data

??? question "What if I'm starting with a SeuratObject?"

    #### Starting with a SeuratObject/Visium HD

    As mentioned previously, [scider](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/scider.html) expects a [SpatialExperiment](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/SpatialExperiment.html) objects. 
    If you have a SeuratObject, you will need to convert it first[^1].

    ```r linenums="1"
    ## Convert to SCE
    sce <- Seurat::as.SingleCellExperiment(seu)
        
    ## Extract spatial coordinates
    spatialCoords <- as.matrix(
        seu@images[[img_id]]@coordinates[, c("imagecol", "imagerow")])

    ## Extract and process image data
    img <- SpatialExperiment::SpatialImage(
        x = as.raster(seu@images[[img_id]]@image))

    imgData <- DataFrame(
        sample_id = sample_id,
        image_id = img_id,
        data = I(list(img)),
        scaleFactor = seu@images[[img_id]]@scale.factors$lowres)

    # Convert to SpatialExperiment
    spe <- SpatialExperiment(
        assays = assays(sce),
        rowData = rowData(sce),
        colData = colData(sce),
        metadata = metadata(sce),
        reducedDims = reducedDims(sce),
        altExps = altExps(sce),
        sample_id = sample_id,
        spatialCoords = spatialCoords,
        imgData = imgData
    )
    # indicate all spots are on the tissue
    spe$in_tissue <- 1
    spe$sample_id <- sample_id
    ```

We'll use the same example data used in the scider documentation[^2]. This is a subset of Xenium Breast Cancer dataset.
```r
spe <- data("xenium_bc_spe") # (1)!
```

1. 
  ```r
  plotSpatial(spe, group.by = "cell_type", pt.alpha = 0.8)
  ```
  ![Spatial plot](data:image/png;base64,)

This data also has 4 annotated cell types:

=== "Table of Cell Types"

    | B cells | Breast cancer | Fibroblasts | T cells |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | 643 | 3550 | 4234 | 1537 |

=== "R code"

    ```r
    table(colData(spe)$cell_type)
    ```

[^1]: Code for converting inspired by [Marc Elosua Bayés](https://github.com/drighelli/SpatialExperiment/issues/115)
[^2]: Li M, Liu N, Nguyen Q, Chen Y (2026). scider: Spatial cell-type inter-correlation by density in R. doi:10.18129/B9.bioc.scider. R package version 1.10.0, https://bioconductor.org/packages/scider.
